name: Nursing Bedside Care & Assessment
description: Evaluates a nurse's spoken English at the bedside: assessing a symptom, orienting a confused or distressed patient, and keeping the patient informed during routine care.

anchors.80-100: Clear, fluent, unhurried phrasing; the patient is never left waiting for a word.
anchors.50-70: Understandable but occasional hesitations or grammar errors.
anchors.10-40: Frequent errors that impede understanding at the bedside.

anchors.80-100: Elicits the specific information the situation requires, using open questions first and closing in on specifics.
anchors.50-70: Covers most of what is needed but relies on closed questions or misses one important dimension.
anchors.10-40: Assessment is thin or leading; the nurse would not be able to report or act on what was gathered.

anchors.80-100: Explains who they are, what they are about to do, and why, in everyday words, before doing it.
anchors.50-70: Explains some actions but performs others without narrating them.
anchors.10-40: Acts without explanation, or explains in clinical register the patient cannot follow.

anchors.80-100: Names and validates the patient's feeling before problem-solving; the patient is treated as a person, not a task.
anchors.50-70: Polite and kind but moves to the task before acknowledging the distress.
anchors.10-40: Ignores or minimizes clearly expressed distress.

anchors.80-100: Stays within nursing scope, is honest about what they can and cannot decide, and says what happens next.
anchors.50-70: Mostly appropriate but over-promises or gives a vague 'I'll see what I can do'.
anchors.10-40: Makes medical decisions or promises outside nursing scope, or leaves without a next step.

checklist.item: Introduced self and role, and said what they were there to do
Used an open question before narrowing to specifics
Gathered the specific information the situation requires
Acknowledged the patient's feeling in words before moving to the task
Explained in plain English what will happen next and roughly when
Stayed within nursing scope and was honest about what needed a doctor's decision
Checked before leaving whether the patient needed anything else
